default.description: Core window permissions. All intelligence lives server-side; the shell only needs its own two settings commands (which are always allowed) plus basic window control. allow-start-dragging is NOT part of core:window:default — without it the data-tauri-drag-region strip silently no-ops (hidden titlebar = unmovable window). opener:allow-open-url MUST carry an explicit url scope — the bare permission enables the open_url command with an EMPTY allow-list, so the plugin rejects every URL with ForbiddenUrl (silent-fail). We scope it to http/https ONLY, matching the http(s)-only guard in src/lib/opener.ts — mailto/tel/file/custom schemes are never handed to the OS shell from email content. Attachment download grants exactly two things: dialog:allow-save (open the native save dialog) and fs:allow-write-file (write the bytes). NO fs scope entry is present, so fs writes are denied for every path EXCEPT the one the user just picked in the save dialog — Tauri auto-adds the dialog-chosen path to the runtime fs scope. This is deliberately the narrowest grant that lets a user save an attachment: no broad fs read, no directory scope, no arbitrary-path write.
